title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 195 (Agent’s duty in naming such person)

content.overview: Section 195 provides that in selecting such agent for his principal, an agent is bound to exercise the same amount of discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; and, if he does this, he is not responsible to the principal for the acts or negligence of the agent so selected.
content.glance: In selecting such agent for his principal, the agent must exercise the same discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; if he does so, he is not responsible for the acts or negligence of the selected agent.
content.study: In selecting such agent for his principal, an agent is bound to exercise the same amount of discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; and, if he does this, he is not responsible to the principal for the acts or negligence of the agent so selected. Current-law framing: duty of care in selection under Section 194; discharge of that duty protects the agent from responsibility for the selected person’s acts or negligence.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: In selecting such agent for his principal, an agent is bound to exercise the same amount of discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; and, if he does this, he is not responsible to the principal for the acts or negligence of the agent so selected.

examples.title: Prudent selection
examples.body: Agent exercises ordinary prudence in selecting a person under Section 194. He is not responsible for that person’s acts or negligence under Section 195.

hypotheticals.question: Agent exercises the discretion of a man of ordinary prudence in selecting the person under Section 194. Is he responsible for that person’s subsequent negligence?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Under Section 195, if he exercises that discretion he is not responsible to the principal for the acts or negligence of the agent so selected.
